correctness.rationale: Frozen RESULT.md bd457202f7234020133eed4e50cf1ef4e8eb30f2 uses Adam-Day--Cameron finite-component theorem: each finite connected simple graph Γ occurs infinitely often as a component. Frucht supplies connected finite Γ with Aut Γ ≅G. A countable disjoint union of Γ has full permutation automorphism group Aut(Γ)^N ⋊ S∞; extending permutations and within-component automorphisms by identity outside the component union embeds this group as the closed pointwise stabilizer of its complement, with correct permutation topology. G=1 gives closed S∞ and its non-local compactness propagates to the larger group. Any countable group embeds abstractly in S∞ via the regular action. Independent exhaustions for unions K2×2, K2×3, K3×2 recovered (q!)^k k!; these only corroborate the finite step. Countability and loop allowance properly handled.

value.rationale: The result determines a uniform, nontrivial topological and subgroup-complexity lower bound for every countable Anti-Foundation double-membership graph despite substantial model-dependent variability. A closed G wr S∞ for every finite G is more informative than merely an arbitrary abstract embedding; this is a motivated structural lemma about natural model-theoretic objects, not an artificial fixed instance.

final_claim: For every countable model of ZFA and every finite group G, Aut of its double-membership graph contains a topologically closed unrestricted wreath product G^N semidirect S_infinity; closed S_infinity implies non-local compactness and every countable abstract subgroup embeds.
limitations: No classification of infinite connected components or complete automorphism group
Conclusions rely on cited finite-component theorem and Frucht connected-graph theorem; limited numerical checks do not prove either.
